title: AI Systems and Useful Work
summary: Recognize what an AI system is, where it can help, and where human judgment remains essential.
objectives: Distinguish artificial intelligence, machine learning, models, and complete AI systems.
Match common AI capabilities to suitable tasks.
Identify the people, data, software, and controls surrounding a model.
Decide when an AI-assisted task needs human review or should not be automated.

sections.title: An AI product is a system, not a magic answer box
paragraphs: Artificial intelligence is a broad term for computer systems that perform tasks associated with perception, prediction, language, planning, or decision support. Machine learning is one way to create AI behavior by learning patterns from examples instead of writing every rule by hand. In production environments, engineers must account for token utilization patterns, context window pressure, and deterministic execution boundaries. When system constraints or rate limits are approached, explicit retry strategies with exponential backoff and jitter prevent cascading failures across downstream dependencies.

A model is only one component. A useful AI system also includes instructions, input data, software, tools, permissions, user experience, monitoring, and people who remain accountable for the outcome. In production environments, engineers must account for token utilization patterns, context window pressure, and deterministic execution boundaries. When system constraints or rate limits are approached, explicit retry strategies with exponential backoff and jitter prevent cascading failures across downstream dependencies.

When evaluating a product, ask what model or method it uses, what information it receives, what actions it can take, and what surrounding controls verify or limit its behavior. In production environments, engineers must account for token utilization patterns, context window pressure, and deterministic execution boundaries. When system constraints or rate limits are approached, explicit retry strategies with exponential backoff and jitter prevent cascading failures across downstream dependencies.
sections.callout: Judge the whole system—including data, tools, people, and controls—not only the model response.

sections.title: Capability patterns help you find appropriate work
paragraphs: Generative systems are often useful for drafting, summarizing, explaining, transforming formats, extracting structure, classifying examples, brainstorming alternatives, and reasoning over material supplied in context. In production environments, engineers must account for token utilization patterns, context window pressure, and deterministic execution boundaries. When system constraints or rate limits are approached, explicit retry strategies with exponential backoff and jitter prevent cascading failures across downstream dependencies.

Other AI systems may rank, recommend, detect patterns, forecast values, transcribe audio, interpret images, or control a physical process. The label AI does not tell you which capability is present or how reliable it is. In production environments, engineers must account for token utilization patterns, context window pressure, and deterministic execution boundaries. When system constraints or rate limits are approached, explicit retry strategies with exponential backoff and jitter prevent cascading failures across downstream dependencies.

A good use case has a clear outcome, suitable data, a way to evaluate quality, and consequences that match the available controls. In production environments, engineers must account for token utilization patterns, context window pressure, and deterministic execution boundaries. sections.title: Assistance and automation are different decisions
paragraphs: An assistant proposes work for a person to inspect. An automated system may act without reviewing every output. The same model can create very different risk depending on whether it drafts a private outline or sends messages, changes records, or controls infrastructure. In production environments, engineers must account for token utilization patterns, context window pressure, and deterministic execution boundaries. When system constraints or rate limits are approached, explicit retry strategies with exponential backoff and jitter prevent cascading failures across downstream dependencies.

Begin with assistance when the task is unfamiliar, evidence is incomplete, or mistakes are costly. Increase automation only after evaluation shows dependable behavior and the surrounding system can limit, observe, and reverse actions. In production environments, engineers must account for token utilization patterns, context window pressure, and deterministic execution boundaries. When system constraints or rate limits are approached, explicit retry strategies with exponential backoff and jitter prevent cascading failures across downstream dependencies.
sections.callout: The right question is not only “Can AI do this?” but “Can this complete system do it safely enough for these consequences?”

sections.title: Human accountability does not disappear
paragraphs: People choose the objective, acceptable risk, data, model, tools, evaluation method, and response when something goes wrong. An AI output can inform a decision, but it cannot accept responsibility for the decision. In production environments, engineers must account for token utilization patterns, context window pressure, and deterministic execution boundaries. High-impact uses need clear ownership, documented review, accessible appeal or correction paths, and evidence that the system performs acceptably for the people and situations it affects. activity.title: Triage four possible AI use cases
instructions: Choose four tasks from work, school, home, or a community activity.
For each task, identify the desired outcome, input data, AI capability, affected people, and consequence of a wrong result.
Classify the first release as no AI, AI assistance with review, limited automation with approval, or automation with monitoring.
Write one verification method and one stop or rollback condition for each task.
evidence: A four-row use-case table containing outcome, data, capability, people, consequence, release mode, verification, and stop condition.
A short explanation of why the highest-risk task receives the strongest human control.
activity.reflectionPrompt: Which task looked easy until you considered the complete system and the consequence of being wrong?

cues.text: Start by replacing the idea of a magic answer box with a system view: model, data, software, tools, controls, and accountable people.
Reveal a model in the center, then add input data, application code, tools, permissions, monitoring, users, and an accountable owner.
cues.accessibilityAlternative: A text list explains that an AI system contains a model plus data, application code, tools, permissions, monitoring, users, and an accountable owner. Reduced-motion mode displays all labels at once.

cues.text: Walk through capability patterns such as generation, extraction, classification, recommendation, perception, and forecasting without treating them as equally reliable.
Pause and name one task where transforming supplied material is more appropriate than asking for an unsupported factual answer.
Contrast a private draft reviewed by a person with an agent that sends a message or changes a record. Emphasize that action changes the risk.
Check that the learner can explain why the same model requires different controls when it moves from proposing to acting.
Close the concept lesson by assigning decisions and consequences to people and organizations rather than to the model.
Guide the learner through the four-use-case triage table and ask them to defend the strongest control.
Invite the learner to complete the knowledge check only after their table includes verification and a stop condition.

questions.prompt: Which description best represents a complete AI system?
choices: A model by itself
A model combined with data, software, tools, controls, users, and accountable people
Any application that produces text
A database containing every correct answer
questions.explanation: The behavior and risk come from the complete system, not from the model alone.

questions.prompt: Which task is generally the strongest starting point for AI assistance?
choices: Automatically approve a high-impact benefit decision
Draft three alternatives from supplied material for a person to review
Delete production records when a response sounds confident
Provide an uncited medical diagnosis
questions.explanation: Drafting alternatives from supplied material has a clear review step and avoids irreversible action.

questions.prompt: What changes most when a workflow moves from assistance to automation?
choices: The spelling of the prompt
The system may act without a person reviewing every output
The model becomes a database
Verification is no longer necessary
questions.explanation: Automation changes who or what acts and therefore increases the importance of permissions, monitoring, and recovery.

questions.prompt: Who remains accountable for selecting and operating an AI-supported process?
choices: The model
The training dataset
The people and organization deploying the system
No one when the output is generated automatically
questions.explanation: People and organizations choose the purpose, controls, and response to harm; the model cannot accept accountability.

questions.prompt: Which set of questions is most useful when evaluating an AI use case?
choices: Is it popular, fast, and visually impressive?
What is the outcome, what data is used, who is affected, what happens if it is wrong, and how is it verified?
Can it remove every human from the process?
Does the product use the largest available model?
questions.explanation: Outcome, data, affected people, consequences, and verification expose whether the complete use case is appropriate.
